authored.summary: How far price has moved, in percent, against where it stood a set number of bars ago, coloured by side of zero
authored.description:
## What it shows
A line in its own pane: the percent change of **Source** (the close by default) against its value **Length** bars earlier (9 by default), `100 × (source − source[length]) ÷ source[length]`. The line is drawn in the **Above zero** colour while the change is zero or positive and in the **Below zero** colour while it is negative, around a dashed zero line. The same change, in **Source**'s own units — rupees for a price **Source**, shares for Volume — appears in the Data Window as **Change**.

## How to read it
- Above zero, price is higher than it was **Length** bars ago; below zero, it is lower.
- The further the line sits from zero, the faster price has moved; a line that flattens while price keeps rising shows momentum slowing.
- A cross of the zero line marks the bar the move over the window turned from a loss to a gain, or back.
- Alerts are available for **Crossed above zero** and **Crossed below zero**.

## Limits
- It compares two single bars, so one unusual close — the one leaving the window as well as the one entering it — can swing the line.
- It has no fixed upper or lower bound, so extremes differ from stock to stock.
- Nothing is drawn until **Length** earlier bars are loaded.
